summary: This PR swaps the placeholder checkbox list for a real quiz screen. A ViewModel loads questions through a new QuestionRepository, which caches the result and uses a Mutex so that two callers loading at the same time share one fetch. Each question shows radio-button answers. On the main thread, which is how it runs today, the logic is correct: the header and the list trigger only one API request. I found two minor issues in the repository, both about keeping that guarantee true later.

accepted.title: The cache shortcut is not safe if the repository is called from more than one thread
accepted.whatGoesWrong: `questions()` first reads `cache` without holding the lock. Today every caller runs on the main thread, so this works. Once someone calls it from a background dispatcher, which is likely when the fake API becomes a real network call, that unlocked read has no memory-visibility guarantee. A thread can see a stale null and fetch again, or in theory see a map that is only partly built.
accepted.whyItMatters: The class exists to guarantee one fetch and a consistent cache. That guarantee quietly breaks under multithreaded use, and the comment suggests that use is planned.
accepted.howToFix: Mark `cache` as `@Volatile`, or drop the unlocked fast path and always read inside `lock.withLock`.

accepted.title: No test checks that loading at the same time makes only one API request
accepted.whatGoesWrong: The main purpose of this PR is that two parts of the screen load questions at the same time but share one request. Nothing tests this. Someone could later delete the second check inside the lock or move the cache write, and both callers would hit the API with nothing failing. The on-screen request counter is the only sign.
accepted.whyItMatters: Once the API is a real backend, a broken cache doubles network traffic and cost without anyone noticing.
accepted.howToFix: Add a unit test using `runTest`. Start two concurrent `questions()` calls against a fake `QuizApi` that counts calls. Assert that it was called exactly once and that both callers got the same map. Optionally add a test that a failed fetch does not leave a bad cache behind.
